name: Cherwell

licensing.selective: No selective licensing scheme: the council’s 2024 HMO licensing policy report says it does not run additional or selective licensing.
licensing.additional: No additional HMO licensing scheme; only national mandatory HMO licensing applies (five or more people from two or more households).

housing: Cherwell's two towns, Banbury and Bicester, have grown fast, with large new-build estates on their edges and garden town development around Bicester. Banbury has Victorian terraces in Grimsbury and post-war estates to the west, while Kidlington provides suburban homes close to Oxford. The north of the district has villages of honey-coloured ironstone cottages, many listed. Heyford Park, on a former RAF base, includes former service housing and new homes.
checkinTips: Ironstone cottages in the northern villages: photograph soft stone, window sills, beams and any damp at the base of walls.
New-build homes in Bicester and Banbury: note snagging marks, sealant around baths and showers, and new garden fences and turf.
Former service houses at Heyford Park: record heating systems, windows and the condition of shared green spaces and parking.
Victorian terraces in Grimsbury: photograph rear extensions, back yards and any damp in older walls.
Rural homes without mains gas: photograph oil tanks, LPG bottles and any septic tank or treatment plant.
Homes near the River Cherwell and the Oxford Canal: check ground floors and gardens for signs of damp or past flooding.
tenantHelp: Tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems in a privately rented home can contact Cherwell District Council's private sector housing team.
